title: Does The Peak-End Rule Apply To Customer Journeys?
summary: Customers whose journeys end on a high note or include a positive surprise are more loyal. Learn how to design and measure memorable moments.
body_markdown:
Yes. Customers whose journeys end on a high and customers whose journeys include a positive surprise are more loyal.


This blog is part of a series on how customer journeys drive loyalty (scroll to the end for all resources).


### Our Data Confirms The Peak-End Rule For Customer Journeys


The peak-end rule states that people judge their experience as the average of how it felt at its peak and at its end. Their memories then determine what they do next. Daniel[Kahneman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Kahneman) and Barbara[Fredrickson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Fredrickson) first described this in 1993 through a study of patients experiencing pain.


Our data shows that customers whose journeys don’t end on a high and who don’t experience positive surprises are less loyal: Among banking customers who did not experience a positive surprise during their journey, the share of very-low-loyalty customers was nearly 10 times higher than among those who did. Similarly, when journeys don’t end on a high note, the share of very-low-loyalty customers is about seven times higher than when they do.


### Design And Measure Highs And Ends Of Customer Journeys


For each journey:


- **Plan for peaks.** Singapore’s Changi Airport created its majestic[Jewel Rain Vortex](https://www.jewelchangiairport.com/) , and[Chewy](https://www.chewy.com/education/forever-loved) decided to send pet owners sympathy cards after their pet dies. But peaks can also be evoked by avoiding industry-typical pain points. For example,[Buc-ee’s](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/samsternjones_turning-negative-experience-peaks-into-positive-activity-7449793154398040064-XTOZ/) has well-maintained and clean bathrooms, differentiating it from other highway rest stops.
- **Level up journey endings.** Walt Disney World and Disneyland added a[car locator function](https://www.ocregister.com/2022/07/12/disneyland-car-finder-helps-remember-where-you-parked/) to their app that directs visitors to their car at the end of the day.


Then, measure journey highs and ends. Use feedback or sentiment analysis to understand whether customers perceive your intended peaks or signature moments as a positive surprise and whether customers feel positive at the end.
